chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from more than one person who narrated it from both of them, all together:

That the slaughtered animal of the woman, if she slaughters well and designates (the name of God), there is no harm in eating it; and likewise the child, and likewise the blind man if he is guided (in his slaughter).
ai.seo_question: Is the meat slaughtered by a woman, child, or blind person permissible to eat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the validity of slaughter (dhabihah) by women, children, and the blind hinges on the proper execution of the act and the recitation of God's name, rather than gender or physical perfection. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor defects in the slaughtering party do not invalidate the meat, provided the essential conditions of *tajwiya* (competence) and *tasmiya* are met. This ruling underscores the accessibility of halal consumption for all Muslims regardless of their physical or social status.
